summary:
I ported perl to the shared README tutorial, root quick start and REFERENCE page by following PORTING v3.2. New files: Naming_perl.ts (22 lines), Syntax_perl.ts (191 lines) and the porter's part of ts/test/runtimeforms/perl.ts (+21 lines). The three old components (735 lines) are deleted. No shared source file changed.

What I ran and what it gave:
- `npm run build`: exit 0, and `git status` was clean afterwards.
- The perl guard: 4/4. runtimefacts plus runtimereader: 65/65.
- The repository suite without generatedcompile, `--test-concurrency=2`: 2601 tests, 2596 pass, 0 fail, 5 skipped.
- The golden: only perl's 5 lines changed.
- The one command: exit 0 with `REGEN=1` and again without it.
- The `SCRATCH=1` run fails, as it must for a new language, because it ignores hand records.
- The perl README example lane (`tools/before/run.sh <clone> perl`), on a copy of oldclone and on mine, gave identical results in all three models (default, crud, basic-server). Every run was 7/7 and exited 0. In the default model: README 18 blocks (17 run, 1 illustration), REFERENCE 21/21 run, root 3/3 run.

On "both modes": I read it as with and without `REGEN=1`. If it means `SCRATCH=1` as well, `ok` is false.

Interface: one gap, additive, and I did not change shared code for it. The imports printer cannot tell the tutorial (read from perl/, OLD `use lib 'lib'`) from the root quick start (read from the repository root, OLD `use lib 'perl/lib'`). The provider therefore prints only `use DemoSDK;`, and I recorded the dropped lib lines by hand.

Purity: 0 open, 1 accepted (exampleVarName). 67 facts, 0 without an account, 0 UNATTESTED after one hand-recorded fact. One runtime note, 9 words.

Against the hypotheses, for perl:
- H1 holds. The provider and hook read the model 0 times, and notes are 1.6% of the page's words. Breaking interface changes: 0.
- H2 holds. 735 lines became 213 (3.45x), or 234 counting the forms additions.
- H3, as far as I read: every catalogued correction perl shows came from shared code with no perl edit (S49, S50, S25, S13, U34, U45, ref-6, md-cell). I did not re-read the catalogue entries.
- H4 holds on the lane: the same counts as OLD. Still, no tool compiled the 153 changed blocks of the 21 variations.

interface_gaps.construct: The page's imports are one printer, `Syntax.imports(desc, used)`, printed ahead of both the tutorial's client block and the root quick start. perl's import line depends on where the reader runs. OLD tutorial (ReadmeQuick_perl.ts:39 at v32-frozen) printed `use lib 'lib';` and OLD root (ReadmeTopQuick_perl.ts:265) printed `use lib '${target.name}/lib';`. The generator's own comment, Main_perl.ts:68-69, says callers write `use lib '<sdk>/lib'; use <Name>SDK;`. Nothing in `desc`, `used` or `Scope` tells the printer which section it is printing, and the provider may not read the target's directory.
interface_gaps.file_line: ts/src/helpers/example.ts:431 (imports signature), :497-500 (printStmts calls imports); ts/src/cmp/ReadmeQuick.ts:183 and :240 (quickText and topQuickText each make a Scope with no place)
interface_gaps.smallest_change: Add an optional `place?: ShowPlace` to Scope. quickText sets 'tutorial' and topQuickText sets 'top', and printStmts passes `sc.place` as a third, optional argument to `imports`. The root path also needs the target's directory: an optional `layout.names` role from the naming hook (`target.name` today; out-of-tree `output.path` targets would need the same). Two shared files (example.ts, ReadmeQuick.ts) plus one optional hook value.
interface_gaps.providers_forced: none (optional argument and optional Scope member; every existing provider ignores them)
interface_gaps.worked_around: Not worked around by branching. Syntax_perl.ts:144-147 prints only `use ${desc.layout.module};` in both places, with a comment saying why. OLD's `use lib 'lib'` (tutorial) and `use lib 'perl/lib'` (root) are dropped, recorded by hand: `dropped` 9b32484fa9, 33526951e8, 336fea9d3b, dc2822fe83, and named in the reason of every block class that also drops them. The first version printed `use lib 'lib'` in both places, which made the root README contradict its own `perl/lib` test block. I removed it as false. Cost: tutorial client blocks byte-identical to OLD went from 3 to 0.

guide_problems.section: 2 / 13 (Imports are a fact of the page)
guide_problems.problem: The guide says imports print once ahead of the tutorial and the root quick start. It does not say that the printer cannot tell which of the two it is in, so a language whose import depends on where the reader runs (perl's `use lib`) cannot express both. Not listed among known limits.

Every constructor line must be derived or cited, but a non-call line such as `use lib 'lib';` has no exact runtime spelling. The only quote is a comment saying `<sdk>/lib`, which passes on word tokens. The guide gives no rule for import lines in `ctor`.

Before `--record-counts`, the one command showed blocks OPEN 1 in tutorial with no line naming the cause (a changed normalizer count). Only the README's table says 'and a changed normalizer count'. The screen should say it.

It does not say that 'fields' changes every print block from OLD's `->{id}` to id plus a display field (sdkdesc showFields). It also does not say that, with no perl normalizer and no reference language using 'fields', the fact is 'not judged' and every such block is a hand class.
It does not say whether reader rows for undocumented members (client TO_JSON on 'module') should be corrected in the forms, or only reported.

'P/base32/oldclone is read-only: the guide's command works on a copy' is ambiguous: tools/before/run.sh reads the clone's dist-test and chdirs into its scaffold. I used a full copy (P/ports/perl/oldcopy) to be safe.

The task's `ok` says the one command must pass 'in both modes'. SCRATCH=1 cannot pass for any newly ported language, because it ignores hand records by design. I read 'both modes' as with and without REGEN=1.
The note lint flags ordinary English words that happen to be entity names in the fixtures ('record'). The guide allows accepting it with a reason; rewording was simpler and is what I did.

Not flagged by the tool, so I declare it myself: Syntax_perl.ts `const scalar = (name) => '$' + name` adds Perl's scalar sigil to description names (Ref.name, sym.var, and the 'options'/'fetchargs' container word). It is used by name(), ref.key, ref.instance and ref.read. I count it as syntax (how Perl writes a variable), not a naming rule. A reviewer may read it as concatenation on a description name.

The attempt printer (Syntax_perl.ts, attempt) shapes its output on the statement: a body opening with a bound call becomes OLD's `my $x = eval { call }; if (my $err = $@) {...} else {...}`. That is a pure function of the statement; it reads no model and tests no operation name.
